questions: What is management's LATEST guidance for the next quarter (revenue, gross margin, operating expenses) and its outlook for the next fiscal year and beyond, with the date each was given; how did earlier guidance compare with what was reported?
What drove the latest reported results (segments, price, volume, mix, costs), and how did they compare with expectations?

What do management and the largest customers say about future demand: order book, backlog or bookings, supply constraints, customers' capex plans, revenue per unit of capacity, customer concentration, and any financing, guarantees or investments the company provides to its customers?
Are earnings flattered or depressed by one-offs: investment gains, impairments, non-GAAP or non-IFRS adjustments, working-capital swings?
Which government policies, taxes, subsidies, export controls or regulations changed recently, and how do they affect the company?

What major corporate events happened in the last four months (acquisitions, bond issues, guarantees, buyback authorisations and how much remains, dividends, management changes, investigations, lawsuits)?
What are the capex and investment plans, and how are they funded?
What is changing in competition, market share, pricing and customers?
Why has the share price moved recently, and what are brokers and the press debating?
Which dated events are coming up (results dates, product launches, policy dates, meetings)?

How much of current data-center demand is underpinned by commitments or financing from a small group of hyperscalers and neocloud customers, and what happens to revenue if their AI capex plans are cut or delayed?
How durable is gross margin given HBM/CoWoS cost pressure, pricing competition from custom ASICs, and any mix shift toward full systems and software?
How are export controls and China-related policy changes affecting NVIDIA's addressable market, product qualifications, and compliance costs, and what is management's latest assumption?
What is the status and funding of the customer/supplier agreements disclosed in recent 8-Ks, and do they create credit, guarantee, or related-party risk?
Are purchase commitments, inventory, and receivables growing faster than revenue, and do non-GAAP adjustments or investment gains obscure cash conversion?

narrative.company_overview:
NVIDIA is a data center scale AI infrastructure company organised into Compute & Networking and Graphics. Its main products span accelerators, networking and software for AI, gaming, workstations and automotive. In FY2026 Data Center was 89.7% of revenue at $193.7bn, Gaming 7.4% at $16.0bn, Professional Visualization 1.5% at $3.2bn, Automotive 1.1% at $2.3bn and OEM & Other 0.3%. The Blackwell Ultra ramp, Grace CPU and Spectrum-X Ethernet drive the data-center franchise, with hyperscale, AI cloud, enterprise and sovereign customers.

The customer and geographic base is concentrated: the United States generated 69.3% of FY2026 revenue, Taiwan 19.6%, and Mainland China & Hong Kong 9.1%. NVIDIA’s competitive position is strong but contested: AMD, Broadcom, Marvell and custom silicon efforts from Microsoft and others target its accelerator share.
narrative.financial_analysis: For the latest reported period, 1H FY2027 revenue rose 95.8% to $177,837mn from $90,805mn; gross margin expanded to 75.0% from 66.6%; operating profit rose 134.2% to $117,270mn. Q2 FY2027 revenue was $96,221mn, up 105.9% year over year. Our forecast: FY2027 revenue $413,521mn, +91.5%, versus consensus $411,653mn; FY2028 $702,986mn, +70.0%, versus $692,206mn; FY2029 $949,031mn, +35.0%. Drivers are expected Q4 hyperscale reacceleration, CPU revenue more than doubling in FY2028 and top-five hyperscaler capex of $1.3tn in 2027. The five-year record shows revenue from $26,914mn in FY2022 to $215,938mn in FY2026, with FY2026 gross margin 71.1%, ROE 101.5% and cash conversion 0.86x; net cash was $23,220mn at 26 July 2026.
narrative.valuation_overview: The rating uses the probability-weighted scenario DCF: fair value $209.61, 16.6% above $179.69. Reverse DCF shows the price embeds 39.1% annual revenue growth versus the model's 41.7% path. Peer multiples are richer: median forward P/E 19.0x versus NVDA 11.3x, and peer P/E implies $301.79. Current P/E on last fiscal-year EPS is 38.1x, at the 6th percentile of a five-year range with median 64.1x. Monte Carlo median is $205.20; 65% of draws above price; P10-P90 is $127.91–$320.45. The rating would turn Sell at or above $232.90.
narrative.competitive_analysis: NVIDIA’s operating performance is far ahead of peers. Latest-quarter revenue growth was +105.9% and latest-quarter operating margin 66.2%; operating comparison gross margin of 74.7% and ROE of 117.2% are trailing twelve months, while Q2 FY2027 gross margin was 75.0%. Peer medians are +40.6% revenue growth, 54.6% gross margin, 18.9% operating margin and 30.4% ROE. Broadcom is closest, with +85.5% revenue growth and 75.5% gross margin. Valuation is split: forward P/E 11.3x is 40.5% below the peer median 19.0x, but P/B 18.9x is 94.5% above peers. NVIDIA’s edge lies in Blackwell Ultra, Spectrum-X Ethernet and Grace CPU; custom-silicon efforts and customer concentration are threats.
narrative.news_summary: Recent news highlights customer efforts to reduce reliance on Nvidia: Microsoft’s Maia 300 aims to cut dependence, and Broadcom’s TPU compute shipments doubled in fiscal Q3 2026. Reports also flag inventory turnover at a multi-year low and a record buyback plan. After the 6 November 2026 price date, Nvidia’s board announced an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after reports of a foreign intelligence effort; shares fell in early 9 November trading, and congressional scrutiny adds export-control risk. The board says it has confidence in the CEO and no known compromise.
narrative.report_summary: Management’s latest outlook, from the Q2 FY2027 call and filings dated 26 and 31 August 2026, guides Q3 FY2027 revenue to $108.0bn, plus or minus 2%, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin to 74.0%, and Q4 gross margin to bottom in the 71% to 72% range before settling at 72% to 73% in FY2028; full-year FY2027 OpEx growth is guided in the low 50s. Management expects approximately 70% supply-constrained growth, Vera Rubin at about 20% of Q3 Data Center revenue, hyperscale growth to reaccelerate in Q4 and into FY2028, and CPU revenue to more than double in FY2028.
